findings.demonstrated_source_property: close conditions all metadata/archive cleanup on not failed. run_phase leaves failed=True when an active terminal turn has status=failed, has no final receipt, or its JSON is invalid.
findings.behavioral_consequence: An already finished root is left unarchived and owned descendants are not updated on these terminal failure paths, although the process is reaped.
findings.requirement_or_engineering_basis: A terminal root must be archived; whether receipt processing succeeds is a separate state from whether the native root finished.
findings.minimal_repair: Track accepted terminal completion independently of failed, gate cleanup on that state and actual root start, and exclude needs-input only when a valid receipt establishes resumability.
findings.proposed_executable_counterexample: Emit actual starts R and owned C, then active completion status=failed. Spy on requests and reap. Assert update(C) and archive(R) occur before reap even though run_phase raises. Current close skips both requests.
findings.evidence_kind: static source trace; counterexample not executed

findings.demonstrated_source_property: The same not-failed gate also treats a successful non-turn driver session as terminal. call_linear uses this driver, sets _root_thread_id through thread/start, and always closes with failed=False; archive_on_close defaults True.
findings.behavioral_consequence: An actual-started ephemeral Linear intake root is archived even though it never had a coordinator turn completion. Root lifecycle is inferred from caller success rather than actual terminal state.
findings.requirement_or_engineering_basis: Archive the terminal root when it finishes; track terminal state independently from transport-call success.
findings.minimal_repair: Use the accepted terminal-root flag described above, so the shared Linear intake driver remains a transport session unless its own terminal turn is observed.

findings.demonstrated_source_property: After steer acknowledgement, post_steer_work accepts item/started events based only on threadId==session_id; it never checks params.turnId. Later the flag rejects the active coordinator receipt.
findings.behavioral_consequence: A delayed command/file/tool event from an older coordinator turn makes the current turn fail even though the active coordinator completion and final receipt are valid.
findings.requirement_or_engineering_basis: Only events belonging to the active coordinator thread/turn may establish its outcome.
findings.minimal_repair: Require the active turnId as well as threadId before counting post-steer work. Keep legacy completion acceptance in the completion matcher, independent from work-event routing.

findings.demonstrated_source_property: The completion matcher raises on any different turn ID once a foreign threadId is excluded; this includes legacy notifications without threadId, and same-thread inactive turns.
findings.behavioral_consequence: An inactive coordinator completion (or legacy child/stale completion for C025) terminates the current run as an error before its legitimate active completion can establish the outcome.
findings.requirement_or_engineering_basis: Only the active coordinator thread/turn may establish the outcome; legacy completion with the active turn ID remains accepted.
findings.minimal_repair: Reject/ignore all nonmatching turn IDs as well as foreign thread IDs before accepting the completion; return None rather than raising for an inactive turn.
findings.proposed_executable_counterexample: During active turn "turn-1" on root R, first emit turn/completed with threadId=R and turn.id="turn-old", then emit the valid active final receipt/completion. Assert the active receipt survives. For C025 repeat with threadId omitted and turn.id="turn-child". Active legacy turn.id="turn-1" must still be accepted.
